title: Ethiopian Butter Chicken
community: Ethiopian households — the kibbeh-rich golden chicken
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Qibe Doro — chicken slowly simmered in abundant kibbeh with onion, garlic, ginger, and mild spices including cardamom and turmeric. Less berbere, more kibbeh — the richest, most indulgent chicken preparation in Ethiopian cooking, and the mildest.
longDesc: Qibe Doro is the Ethiopian answer to a butter chicken — not spicy with tomato cream, but rich and golden with kibbeh, fragrant with cardamom and ginger. The chicken is simmered in a generous quantity of kibbeh, producing an extraordinarily rich, unctuous sauce.
ingredients: ½ cup water or chicken stock
// Optional: 2 tbsp yogurt or ayib stirred in at the end
steps: Add kibbeh — all 4 tablespoons. Melt and coat onions.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, cardamom, and pepper. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chicken. Coat in the kibbeh sauce.
Add water or stock. Simmer covered 40—45 minutes.
The sauce should be rich, golden, and slightly oily — this is correct.
Stir in yogurt or ayib at the very end if using.
chefTips: 4 tablespoons of kibbeh is correct — the richness is the point.
The resulting sauce will look oily — this is traditional and correct.
Cardamom is the key aromatic here — use a generous amount.
commonMistakes: Too little kibbeh — loses the characteristic richness.
cookingScience: Kibbeh's spice infusion (see ETH092) means every tablespoon of kibbeh carries the flavours of its infused spices — when 4 tablespoons are used, the sauce becomes a concentrated expression of these aromatics, producing the characteristic Qibe Doro fragrance.
sustainabilityTips: Bone-in chicken — maximum flavour from secondary cuts.
healthBenefits: Kibbeh provides vitamins A, D, E from the spice infusion.
culturalNote: Qibe Doro is the chicken of abundance — when kibbeh is available in plenty, this is what Ethiopian cooks make to demonstrate their generosity. The golden richness of the sauce is the richness of the host's hospitality.
